samples.xml_description:
<module id="freq_divbyfrac">
	<!-- Description goes here. -->
    <description>A frequency divider that divides the input clock frequency by fractional values. It generates a clock signal with a fractional frequency division (3.5x), using the double-edge clocking technique to achieve half-integer division while adjusting for duty cycle imbalance. By dividing uneven clock cycles and phase-shifting them, a smooth fractional clock output is produced.</description>
	
	<ports>
		<input id="clk">Input clock signal.</input>
		<input id="rst_n">Active low reset signal to initialize the module.</input>
		
		<output id="clk_div">Fractionally divided clock output.</output>
	endports
	
	<implementation>Double-edge clocking technique used to generate a fractional clock output from an input clock. The module counts clock cycles up to MUL2_DIV_CLK (which equals 7 for a 3.5x division). Two uneven clock periods are created: one with 4 source clock cycles and another with 3 source clock cycles. In the next cycle, phase-shifted versions of the divided clock are generated, with one being delayed by half a clock period and the other being advanced by half a clock period. These phase-shifted clocks are then OR-ed together to produce the final fractional divided clock output.</implementation>
	
	<parameter_description>
		<!-- Define parameters such as states or named constants here if needed. -->
	</parameter_description>
	
	<logic_description>
		<!-- Signal-level descriptions go here. -->
		<!-- Sequential logic example -->
		<reg type="sequential_logic" id="state_reg" width_description="[2:0]">
			<description>Sequential logic register to hold the current state.</description>
		</reg>
		
		<wire type="combinational_logic" id="next_state_wire" width_description="[2:0]">
			<description>Combinational logic wire to determine the next state.</description>
		</wire>
		
		<always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
			if (!rst_n) begin
				state_reg <= 3'b0;
			end else begin
				state_reg <= next_state_wire;
			end
		end
		
		// Combinational logic example
		assign next_state_wire = /* Your combinational logic here */ 3'b0;
	endlogic_description
	
	<!-- Task definitions go here. -->
</module>
